recipes.name: Lemon Poppy Seed Chicken Pasta Salad
ingredients_raw: 1.5 cups creamy poppy seed salad dressing

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add penne and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain, then rinse under cold water until pasta is cold; drain well.
Combine penne, chicken, celery, cranberries, and green onions in a large bowl; pour in salad dressing and lemon juice and stir until evenly mixed.

raw_recipe.headline: Lemon Poppy Seed Chicken Pasta Salad
raw_recipe.description: This lemon poppy seed chicken pasta salad recipe features penne pasta, chicken, crunchy veggies, dried cranberries, and a creamy poppyseed dressing.

review.reviewBody: Very Good. I used shredded chicken instead of cubes. Also added some toasted slivered almonds, minced red onion and minced red and orange bell pepper.

I served this for FOL lunch. It made a lot more than I expected. It could have used some extra chicken.
I added bacon and about 1 c shredded swiss cheese. I also added some pepper and a little dressing in the morning before serving.
I seasoned and baked the chicken. Then cut it into strips then tore it into pieces

I followed recipe, but didn't add the green onions, and used Rotisseree chicken instead. I also used 1 cup of the Brianna's Poppyseed dressing, very yummy! Then added 1/2 cup al dente broccolli, then 1 cup of blueberries! Perfect!

We really liked this the first time I made it, but some people aren't fond of celery. The next time I made it I substituted 1 cup toasted slivered almonds for the celery and it was a big hit with everyone. This is a great recipe to take to a potluck.

We really liked this the first time I made it, but some people aren't fond of celery. The next time I made it I substituted 1 cup toasted slivered almonds for the celery and it was a big hit with everyone. This is a great recipe to take to a potluck.

Sounded great so I chose to make it for a cookout. Yum! I did add to it tho - Cheese that I cubed, sliced olives, then I cut up (small pieces)steamed broccoli - cooled. I added a little more dressing since I added more veggies (& broccoli soaks up liquid!)So delicious and I was asked to make for Memorial Day Cookout as well! I might add slightly sauteed zucchini &/or summer squash next time!

This was a fabulous dish! I made it for my sister and a picnic her boyfriend was planning for her. I read the reviews and decided to add the juice of one fresh lemon to 2 1/2 cups of dressing. I reserved 1/2 cup for right before serving to moisten the salad. Harris Teeter also has precooked packages of grilled chicken that made this recipe even easier. I am thinking about trying to add lemon zest next time. I am always looking for different and unique pasta salad recipes. This one is definitely a keeper!

So easy, and very flavorful. The poppyseed dressing was perfect with the cranberries. I added a few raisins simply b/c I didn't have enough cranberries and it was very good. Will make again and again.
Easy and very good. I used rotisserie chicken from the supermarket deli.
How does one make the lemon poppyseed dressing?

this was soooo good. a nice change from traditional pasta salad. I added a few slivered almonds for a little more crunch. easy to make also. big hit at the picnic (and no mayo to worry about in the heat). i also used the rotisserie chicken from the store
We don't eat much meat, so I used garbanzo beans instead of chicken. Every last bite was gone!
This was awesome!! I made it exactly like the recipe. No need for any changes. I was afraid I made too much for my family of four, but it didn't last long in the fridge!!
Followed the recipe exactly turn out great, very good! I've made this a few times and every time I have lots of requests for the recipe
Good salad recipe. I didn't have to change a thing.

i love this recipe! i've made it many times, and it's nice for outdoors picnics, because there's no mayo, it doesnt need refrigeration (of course overnight, it's better). I omit the lemon juice and celery, and add crushed walnuts. I also ran a bit short on the dressing, so keep that in mind. one downside (and there's no way to avoid it) is that it doesn't refrigerate that well... it's fine for a day or two, but the penne really soaks up the dressing, and it can get a little dry. just keep that in mind, because this makes a lot of yummy salad!
5 stars isn't enough! It's flippin awesome.
